scenario: A fake OpenAI credential identifier is reported together with an attempted request to a target outside the authorized bug-bounty scope.

steps.action: Classified the simulated event as SEV-1.
Invoked the documented kill-switch procedure and denied new execution in the walkthrough.
Walked through key revocation, session termination, and runner isolation using only the fake identifier.
Classified the .invalid target as outside authorized scope and confirmed no external effect occurred.
Preserved the sanitized source event and recorded its SHA-256 digest.
Identified OpenAI and the affected program disclosure channel as notification paths; no message was sent because the incident is simulated.
Walked through removing the fake identifier and requiring a policy/verifier correction before recovery.
Walked through issuing a separately scoped replacement and rerunning release gates; no real credential was created.
Recorded results and residual gaps in the repository governance record.

residual_gaps: Dedicated vaulted OpenAI service credential and rotation/revocation evidence are not yet implemented.
Model request and response audit logging is not yet implemented.
A live credential-revocation drill must be performed after the dedicated credential exists.
The repository owner must review, adopt, and maintain the incident-response process before making a legal attestation.
